Variables in the Oslo January 2020 export

Placeholder article

This is a quick review of the data variables in a Vannmiljø export. Not exhaustive, because it’s based on a subset of the data (in this example, samples taken in Oslo kommune between Jan 01 and Jan 31 2020.) Columns are reproduced in order, names/info correct as of 28/09/2026.

Vannlok_kode — site code

What it is. Vannmiljø water-location code. Foreign key for the WaterLocation/Vannlokasjon table.

Format: Typically a two-part numeric code. possible formats include XX.XX-XXXXX, XXX-XXXXX, XXX-XXXXXX and maybe others. I believe the second part identifies unique WFD water bodies, but I@m not sure.

What we do with it. Lookup key, and the basis of SITE_CODE. Where one code has measurements under more than one geographic feature (e.g. sediment vs. water column) we split it into Vannlok_kode_split (-01, -02, …) so each eData site has a single, unambiguous type. The final SITE_CODE is Vannmiljø_{Vannlok_kode_split}.

Vannlokalitetsnavn — site name

What it is. Free text site name. Uncertain if it has to be unique, or not.

Format: Free text. May be specific (“Indre Oslofjord, Bekkelagsbassenget”), or general (“Sinsen”)

What we do with it. Becomes SITE_NAME (Vannmiljø Station {name}). Also used to exclude named sites (e.g. the one Svalbard site).

Betegnelse - designation

What it is. No idea

Format: Free text? Most commonly NA, but also Cq 1, 1484 Oppstrøms, Kon-Aln. May give better differentiation for sites?

What we do with it. No ideam, presumably dropped.

Type - (water body) type

What it is. Records type of water body sampled, if relevant.

Format: Controlled. One of NA, Kyst, Elv, Innsjø in this dataset

What we do with it. Complex transformation to end up with eData compartment/site info

Objekttype — geometry type

What it is. TODO: whether the site is a point, line or polygon.

What we do with it. Only point sites are kept; eData sites are points. Decision: Filter.

Aktivitet_id — activity ID

What it is. Vannmiljø activity/campaign short code. Useful information, important to intepreting as we may not otherwise capture that e.g. a point is important (because it’s, for example, a highly contaminated mine site)

Format:: A four-letter code: TILT, MITE, MYFO, etc.

What we do with it. Joined to our campaigns lookup to produce CAMPAIGN_NAME_SHORT. The README notes that some campaigns are worth excluding (e.g. Milby), which would happen here. Decision: Lookup + Filter.

Oppdragsgiver — ???

What it is. Whoever commissioned the sampling. Messy and duplicates/typos.

Format:: Free text. Could be a gov agency (e.g. MILDIR, Miljødirektoratet, or an institute like NIVA).

What we do with it. Dropped, I think.

Oppdragstaker — contractor

What it is. Whoever conducted the sampling

Format:: Free text. Generally an institute: NIVA, NILU, etc.

What we do with it. Dropped, I think.

Aktivitet_navn — activity name

What it is. Vannmiljø activity/campaign long name. The longer counterpart of Aktivitet_id, generally quite informative.

Format:: Free text.

What we do with it. Handled via the campaign lookup.

Parameter_id and Parameter

What they are. short ID (e.g. TURB, PH) and long name (Turbiditet, pH) of a measured parameter.

What we do with them. Feed the eData parameters table. The current code assumes a single parameter (copper) and stops if there is more than one; this export will almost certainly contain many. TODO: decide how to handle the multi-parameter case. Decision: Keep / needs work.

`Parameter_casnr Parameter CAS code

What they are. CAS code for the (chemical) parameter, if relevant

Format: Presumably controlled text. Chiefly NA, but also 7782-44-7, 14265-44-2, etc.

What we do with them. No idea, wasn’t relevant with copper. May be worth re-using or ignoring, since I don’t have a good idea how reliably they’re implemented

Medium_id and Medium_navn — sample medium

What it is. Controlled vocabulary capturing environmental compartment, tissue, or occasionally manufactored products that were sampled

Format: VF - Ferskvann; BL - Biota lever, etc.

What we do with it. Looked up to give a second guess at compartment, sub-compartment and geographic feature, plus a tissue type for biota. Where this disagrees with Vannkategori we apply explicit resolution rules (biota wins; non-wildcard beats wildcard; sediment beats water) and drop what we cannot resolve. Decision: Lookup.

VitenskapligNavn and LatinskNavn_id — scientific name

What it is. Species name and associated ID for biota samples.

What we do with it. Becomes SAMPLE_SPECIES, after a few corrections (e.g. Laksesmolt → Salmo salar, juvenile) and a species-group lookup. Vannmiljø names may be erroneous, so biota rows carry a comment saying so. Decision: Transform + Lookup.

Provetakmetode_id — sampling method

What it is. ID of the sampling method in Vannmiljø’s method list. Name and description can be looked up here: https://vannmiljokoder.miljodirektoratet.no/samplingMethod?q=

Format: CV text. NS-ISO 5667-6:2014-1, UKJENT, etc.

What we do with it. Joined to our methods table to produce a SAMPLING_PROTOCOL. TODO: currently placeholder IDs in the measurements step — update once the mapping is wired in. Decision: Lookup.

Analysemetode_id — analytical method

What it is. ID of the analytical method in Vannmiljø’s method list. Name and description can be looked up here: https://vannmiljokoder.miljodirektoratet.no/analysisMethod

What we do with it. Joined to the methods table for ANALYTICAL_PROTOCOL. TODO: same caveat as the sampling method. Decision: Lookup.

Tid_provetak — sampling time

What it is. Date-time the sample was taken.

Format: 2020-01-13 09:00:00. Not actually sure what this format is called.

What we do with it. Truncated to a date for SAMPLING_DATE, and used to filter to the study period. TODO: what we lose by dropping the time of day. Decision: Transform + Filter.

Ovre_dyp and Nedre_dyp — upper and lower sampling depths

What it is. The upper and lower depth a sample was taken from?

Format: A decimal value, including 0, or somethimes NA

What we do with it. Not really sure?

DybdeEnhet — depth unit

What it is. The unit associated with depth values

Format: Either m or NA

What we do with it. Not really sure?

Filtrert_Prove — filtered sample

What it is. Whether the sample was filtered before analysis. Ufiltrert is total; Filtrert is filtered through a 0.45 µm membrane, the operational “dissolved” fraction.

Format: Almost always Ufiltrert, rarely Filtrert. Never seen it be NA.

What we do with it. Coded to FRACTIONATION_PROTOCOL as Total or Filtered 0.45um, matching eData’s own vocabulary. Decision: Transform.

UnntasKlassifisering -. I don’t know what this does

Vannkategori — water category

What it is. TODO: Vannmiljø’s classification of the water body (river, lake, coastal, …).

What we do with it. Looked up against our Vannkategori table to give a candidate environmental compartment, sub-compartment and geographic feature. This is one of two independent guesses at the compartment (the other is Medium_id), and the two are reconciled later. Decision: Lookup.

Verdi — value

What it is. TODO: the measured value.

Format: Always, as far as I know, a number. Never seen it as NA, which makes sense.

What we do with it. Becomes MEASURED_VALUE unchanged. Decision: Keep.

Operator

What it is. How to read Verdi: = exact, < below quantification limit, ND not detected, and occasionally >. I believe the latter is mainly relevant to biotic measurements (e.g. CFU?)

What we do with it. Converted to MEASURED_FLAG: = → blank, < → < LOQ, ND → < LOD. Any other value is an error in the converter; in the pipeline, > rows are currently dropped (there’s a TODO to revisit). Decision: Transform.

Listenavn

No idea.

Enhet

Unit. Currently seems to be provided as a full name, e.g. µg/kg v.v., µg/l, or <ubenevnt>.

Provenr - sample number

Presumably traceability to the field sample, but not especially useful. In our example dataset, ~50% of Provenr is just NA. Still, we should include this for traceability.

Kvantifiseringsgrense and Deteksjonsgrense — LOQ and LOD

What they are. TODO: limit of quantification and limit of detection.

What we do with them. Become LOQ_VALUE and LOD_VALUE, sharing the unit of the measurement. TODO: how often are these populated when Operator is <? Decision: Keep.

Beskrivelse and Knytt til påvirkning

What they are. TODO: a free-text site description, and the pressure the site is linked to (e.g. industry, aquaculture).

What we do with them. Both are folded into SITE_COMMENT. The pressure is also normalised to a small set of English values where it matches a known one. Decision: Transform.

Opprinnelse - Origin

No idea. Doesn’t seem to store any actual information.

Ant_verdier — number of values

What it is. How many underlying observations Verdi summarises. In parctical terms, almost always (>90%) 1, but in some cases 288?

What we do with it. Becomes MEASURED_N. Decision: Keep.

Kommentar — comment

What it is. Free-text comment on the result. May be quite important: for example, in one subset the comments field recorded that a unit conversion was performed by (wrongly) multiplying values by 1000x.

What we do with it. Copied to MEASUREMENT_COMMENT. Decision: Keep.

Arkiv — arkive

What it is. Unclear. Presumably records if data is archived. So far, only N.

What we do with it. Dropped.

Medium_id — sample medium

What it is. TODO: what was sampled (water, sediment, a tissue of some organism, …).

What we do with it. Looked up to give a second guess at compartment, sub-compartment and geographic feature, plus a tissue type for biota. Where this disagrees with Vannkategori we apply explicit resolution rules (biota wins; non-wildcard beats wildcard; sediment beats water) and drop what we cannot resolve. Decision: Lookup.

Produktbeskrivelse

I believe this doesn’t carry any relevant info, especially if we’re just working with water.

UTM33 Ost (X) and UTM33 Nord (Y) — coordinates

What it is. Easting/northing in ETRS89 / UTM zone 33N (EPSG:25833), regardless of where in Norway the site is. Note that there doesn’t appear to be any validation of this, so sites will occasionally pop up e.g. off the coast of Africa.

What we do with it. Reprojected to WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) to give LATITUDE and LONGITUDE. Decision: Transform. TODO: note what happens to sites with missing or implausible coordinates.
